topic: Honest adaptation to weak non-Gaussianity in structure-agnostic partially linear inference. In the bounded/sub-Gaussian JMS partially linear class with eta independent of X, unit variance, supplied L8 nuisance errors epsilon_g,n and epsilon_q,n, require one interval to be honest over the union of eta exactly Gaussian and |kappa_4(eta)|>=delta_n. Characterize the coordinatewise Pareto lower boundary of Gaussian and non-Gaussian worst-case expected lengths. With s_n=n^-1/2+epsilon_g,n^4, d_n=n^-1/2+epsilon_g,n epsilon_q,n and B_n=n^-1/2+epsilon_g,n^3 epsilon_q,n+epsilon_g,n^4, construct a split cumulant-test plus unnormalized DML/cubic-ACE inversion attaining (d_n,min{d_n,B_n/delta_n}) when delta_n/s_n diverges. Prove matching branch-designated fuzzy-Hermite lower bounds: below s_n no shortening from d_n, and above it strict shortening occurs exactly when B_n/delta_n=o(d_n). Retain any necessary Gaussian logarithms. Do not claim improvement of global union-supremum length; use the vector frontier as the rate-level object, recognizing that the absolute cross-modulus is symmetric and fixed positive-weight scalarizations are rate-degenerate. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolve derived the exact unnormalized DML bias identity E[(Y-qhat)(T-ghat)]-theta_0=E[(ghat-g_0)(qhat-q_0)], the cubic identity E[eta(eta^3-3eta-kappa_3)]=kappa_4, and a split test/intersection construction with non-Gaussian length at most B_n/delta_n+d_n(s_n/delta_n)^2. It solved epsilon_g=epsilon_q=delta_n=n^-1/8, giving lengths n^-1/4 and n^-3/8, and checked the Gaussian-mixture witness has squared Hellinger distance of order delta_n^2. It also found no current-paper or bank collision. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Build a fuzzy-Hermite pair with bounded n-sample chi-square distance that obeys the exact PLM residual law and L8 nuisance budgets while hiding an epsilon_g^4 cumulant signal and sustaining target displacement min{d_n,B_n/delta_n}. EARLY KILL TEST: Solve the finite Rademacher-partition exponential-Hermite two-prior program and require a certified feasible pair at separation comparable to epsilon_g^4+n^-1/2; failure after optimizing partition size and moment-matched nuisance priors should stop the sharp converse. open_problems.why_unsolved: Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis analyze Gaussian and non-Gaussian point-estimation classes separately: the ACE result fixes a cumulant order and assumes its identifying cumulant is bounded away from zero. When |κ_4|=δ_n shrinks, residual fourth-cumulant estimation has error n^-1/2+ε_g,n^4, and selecting DML versus cubic ACE can invalidate uniform coverage. Cai and Low provide the expected-length framework, but their scalar Gaussian experiments do not yield a branch-designated PLM modulus; here the symmetric cross-modulus makes global union-supremum length and fixed positive-weight scalarizations rate-degenerate. The prior finite-support constructions indicate how to preserve common observed support, but the first changed step is a moment-matched exponential-Hermite perturbation that simultaneously enforces η independent of X, the exact PLM residual law, L8 nuisance budgets, and bounded product chi-square distance.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform-coverage upper theorem and matching fuzzy-Hermite converse proving the Pareto boundary (d_n,min{d_n,B_n/δ_n}) when δ_n/(n^-1/2+ε_g,n^4) diverges, no shortening below that testing scale, and strict non-Gaussian shortening exactly when B_n/δ_n=o(d_n), with necessary Gaussian logarithms retained.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The separated-regime construction only needs a cumulant test with vanishing misclassification probability, whereas at δ_n/s_n approaching a finite constant the selector has nondegenerate errors that interact with interval inversion and expected length. Fixed-order ACE bounds do not determine this transition experiment, and ordinary pretest calculations do not guarantee honesty after selection. The prior proposal highlights the analogous observed-law obstacle: a latent branch distinction may cease to be testable unless the close alternatives satisfy every model coupling. Here the first changed proof step is a local asymptotic characterization of the contaminated empirical fourth cumulant under exact-Gaussian and contiguous Hermite alternatives.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem indexed by λ=lim δ_n/s_n that gives the attainable two-coordinate expected-length boundary for every finite λ, an honest split-test/inversion procedure attaining it, and contiguous PLM experiments proving the matching lower boundary.

writing_exemplar.why: Its Gaussian-barrier versus cumulant-opportunity framing makes the unresolved local transition mathematically and practically visible.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Gaussian noise blocks higher-order improvement -> a separated cumulant enables ACE -> weak cumulants approach the detection boundary -> characterize honest inference throughout the local transition.

method_exemplars.technique: Use between-class moduli and tests whose errors remain explicit rather than asymptotically negligible.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The ACE hierarchy is oracle-indexed: choosing r requires knowing which κ_{r+1} is detectably nonzero, while cumulant-estimation constants grow quickly with r and the residual cumulant tests are dependent. Selecting r and estimating the score polynomial on the same observations can invalidate orthogonality and coverage. Gaussianity is also the common intersection at which every higher cumulant vanishes, so a converse must hide several cumulant alternatives simultaneously rather than reuse a fixed-order two-class argument. The located literature contains fixed-order ACE and higher-order orthogonality results but no multiscale honest PLM interval indexed by the unknown first nonzero cumulant.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving the minimax coordinatewise expected-length vector over the Gaussian class and classes {|κ_{r+1}|≥δ_{r,n}}, 2≤r≤R_n, together with a multiplicity-calibrated split cumulant selector/ACE inversion and matching multi-prior lower bounds identifying unavoidable logarithmic and order-growth penalties.

writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Higher-order orthogonality suppresses nuisance bias -> each ACE order requires a corresponding nonzero cumulant -> the useful order and separation are unknown -> build honest multiscale adaptation across the cumulant hierarchy.

open_problems.why_unsolved: ACE cancellation uses a cumulant polynomial centered for the treatment residual law and generally requires conditional centering given X. Under η-X dependence, an unconditional cumulant no longer cancels the conditional Gateaux derivatives, while estimating conditional cumulants introduces another structure-agnostic nuisance that may erase the gain. Existing near-independence results are fixed-order and do not provide honest adaptation over an unknown violation radius. A preliminary independence test followed by ACE is not automatically uniformly valid, so the missing object is a joint frontier in cumulant strength δ_n and dependence radius τ_n with DML retained as the safe branch.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For a stated dependence metric such as τ_n=max_{j≤4}||κ_j(η|X)-Eκ_j(η)||_2, a resolution would give a uniformly honest DML/ACE confidence procedure and matching lower bounds characterizing expected length as a function of (δ_n,τ_n,ε_g,n,ε_q,n,n), including the regime where dependence bias eliminates ACE shortening.

writing_exemplar.why: Its robustness-versus-efficiency framing and warning against pretesting provide the right narrative for treating η independent of X as an uncertain strengthening assumption.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A strong assumption permits a more precise estimator -> the size of its violation is unknown -> pretesting can lose validity or perform poorly -> adapt the interval to both non-Gaussian strength and dependence misspecification.

method_exemplars.technique: Start from the conditional cumulant-polynomial orthogonality identity and replace unconditional centering by an estimated or bias-bounded conditional cumulant correction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The first proof step failing under the destination regime is conditional centering of the ACE score.

method_exemplars.technique: Use cross-fitted first-order orthogonal DML as the uniformly valid safe component and derive its limit law jointly with the corrected ACE score.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The interval must retain coverage whenever the assumption-sensitive higher-order moment is unusable.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt minimax robustness-efficiency optimization to combine safe and assumption-sensitive procedures under an unknown violation radius.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Recent sharp PLM theory shows that deterministic total-error balls conceal asymmetry between approximation error and stochastic learner complexity, and calibrated editing can improve DML for imbalanced learners. ACE residual-cumulant control must instead hold conditionally on random fitted nuisances, while learner editing can contaminate cumulant testing unless independent splitting or stability is imposed. The prior reviewer identifies the portability defect precisely: a theorem stated only through supplied rates lacks a primitive learner class or attainable example. The first new proof step is therefore an observable, uniformly valid L8 error certificate that remains sharp enough when propagated through both branch selection and interval inversion; ordinary validation risk need not upper-bound conditional L8 error at the honesty scale.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sufficient-condition theorem for named primitive nuisance learners that constructs observable high-probability L8 certificates and proves a closed-form Gaussian/non-Gaussian expected-length frontier in their approximation budgets, stochastic complexities, δ_n, and n, or a matching impossibility theorem establishing an unavoidable certification penalty.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Scalar ACE uses a global coefficient θ_0. Replacing it by θ_0(X) requires localization, and θ_0(X)-θ_0(x_0) enters the score as an additional bias, so the exact ACE moment cancellation must be combined with local-polynomial reproduction and bandwidth control. Kennedy et al. supply localized fuzzy-hypothesis and minimax estimation machinery but not distributional inference, while Jin et al. explicitly leave heterogeneous-effect exploitation of non-Gaussianity open. Existing CATE confidence theory does not identify an honest Gaussian/non-Gaussian expected-length frontier driven by a weak residual cumulant.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A pointwise CATE theorem giving Gaussian and |κ_4|≥δ_n minimax expected-length coordinates, an honest localized DML/cubic-ACE interval with a stated limit law and bandwidth, and a matching localized fuzzy-Hermite lower bound identifying exactly when non-Gaussian shortening is possible.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames pointwise CATE as a regression-functional hybrid, derives an elbow-shaped minimax problem, and explicitly motivates inference as the next step.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CATE is a central causal target -> pointwise difficulty combines regression and functional estimation -> current minimax work stops at estimation rates -> ask whether treatment-noise cumulants create a new honest-inference elbow.

method_exemplars.technique: Localize the R-learner or higher-order pseudo-outcome with a local polynomial and adapt its localized fuzzy-hypothesis construction to confidence-length lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies both the destination estimator geometry and the pointwise localization required for θ_0(x_0).

method_exemplars.technique: Insert the cumulant polynomial into a localized orthogonal score and split cumulant estimation from pointwise target inversion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its ACE construction is the direct source of higher-order nuisance insensitivity, while localization is the first proof component that changes.

method_exemplars.technique: Use honest sample splitting and Hájek-projection asymptotic normality as a benchmark for pointwise CATE limit theory and variance estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides an established route from a localized heterogeneous-effect estimator to a centered Gaussian limit and confidence interval.

literature_map:
Robinson (1988, Econometrica, DOI 10.2307/1912705) supplies the foundational partially linear model and root-n semiparametric benchmark.
Chernozhukov et al. (2018, The Econometrics Journal, DOI 10.1111/ectj.12097) establish cross-fitted Neyman-orthogonal DML and valid Gaussian inference under nuisance product-rate conditions.
Mackey, Syrgkanis, and Zadik (2018, ICML, arXiv:1711.00342) prove that second-order orthogonal PLM moments exist exactly when treatment residuals are non-Gaussian.
Balakrishnan, Kennedy, and Wasserman (2023, arXiv:2305.04116) formalize structure-agnostic lower bounds and the general first-order-versus-structure tradeoff.
Jin and Syrgkanis (2025, COLT, arXiv:2402.14264) prove structure-agnostic optimality of doubly robust learning for ATE, ATT, and weighted targets.
Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis (2025, NeurIPS, arXiv:2507.02275) prove the Gaussian PLM barrier and fixed-order ACE rates under a cumulant bounded away from zero; this is the closest anchor.
Jin and Syrgkanis (2026 version, arXiv:2512.17341) develop general fuzzy-hypothesis structure-agnostic lower bounds but do not address honest adaptation across noise classes.
Gu (2026, arXiv:2607.21541) and Hu and Simchi-Levi (2026, arXiv:2609.07997) sharpen PLM point risk by separating approximation from stochastic learner error; neither treats cumulant adaptation or confidence-length frontiers.
Zheng, Bonvini, and Guo (2025, arXiv:2511.01222) obtain valid nonparametric-length inference by perturbing, filtering, and unioning DML intervals, providing a nearby inference construction without non-Gaussian gains.
Cai and Low (2004, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:math/0503662) make between-class and ordered moduli the canonical benchmark for honest adaptive expected length over unions.
Cai and Low (2011, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1105.3039) provide close lower-bound machinery through composite fuzzy hypotheses, moment-matched priors, Hermite approximation, and mixture chi-square control.
Armstrong and Kolesár (2018, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA14434; 2020, Quantitative Economics, arXiv:1606.01200) show how bias-aware minimax theory yields honest scalar confidence intervals.
Armstrong, Kline, and Sun (2025, Econometrica, arXiv:2305.14265) cast unknown misspecification as a robustness-efficiency adaptation problem and document the danger of pretesting.
Quessy and Mailhot (2011, Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference, DOI 10.1016/j.jspi.2011.03.003) analyze skewness and kurtosis tests under contiguous raw-sample alternatives, but not residuals with black-box nuisance error.
Kennedy et al. (2024, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2203.00837) give localized fuzzy lower bounds and minimax pointwise CATE estimation while leaving inference open; Wager and Athey (2018, JASA, arXiv:1510.04342) provide a contrasting pointwise CATE CLT.
